en.title: Maithili Print and Literary Institutions
en.summary: Print did not create Maithili literature. It changed the material conditions under which literature could be copied, standardised, debated, sold, archived and made visible to readers who were not gathered in the same court, school, household or manuscript circle. That distinction is essential for a socio-cultural-economic history. The transition from manuscript to print was not a clean replacement of one technology by another, and the modern literary public was not produced by presses alone.

mai.title: मैथिली मुद्रण आ साहित्यिक संस्थान
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “मैथिली मुद्रण आ साहित्यिक संस्थान” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Print reorganised literary authority; it did not mark the beginning of Maithili literature
Manuscript, oral and print cultures overlapped for generations
Colonial-era printing altered the economics of literary reproduction
The early twentieth-century periodical created a new rhythm of public argument

en.title: Angika Print and Literary Institutions
en.summary: Angika literary modernity cannot be reconstructed by starting from a list of organisations and projecting their categories backward. The speech forms now grouped under the name Angika long preceded the institutions that printed, classified and taught them. Modern print changed something different: it created repeatable editions, editorial norms, periodical rhythms, bibliographies, institutional offices and archives through which a regional literary field could recognise itself and argue about its boundaries.

mai.title: अंगिका मुद्रण आ साहित्यिक संस्थान
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “अंगिका मुद्रण आ साहित्यिक संस्थान” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: The history of modern Angika print is not the beginning of Angika language or expressive culture
Naming and classification became part of print politics
Oral literature entered print through collection, selection and transcription
Bihar Rashtrabhasha Parishad publications provided an early state-supported platform for Angika study

en.title: Radio and Broadcasting
en.summary: Radio changed the scale and temporality of public culture in Mithila, Vajji and Anga. Print required a physical copy and a reader; broadcasting could carry a voice, song, agricultural advisory, drama, news bulletin or political speech across many households at once. Yet the existence of a transmitter did not create a single regional public.

mai.title: रेडियो आ प्रसारण
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “रेडियो आ प्रसारण” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Radio made simultaneity a new social resource
Broadcasting entered a landscape already structured by oral performance and print
Akashvani Patna supplied an early post-independence regional platform
Akashvani Bhagalpur created a durable broadcast node for Anga

en.title: Cinema, Video and Recorded Performance
en.summary: Cinema and recorded performance transformed regional culture in a different way from radio. Broadcasting organised a schedule around a transmitter; moving images and recordings created objects that could be replayed, copied, sold, carried across borders and watched outside the moment of performance. For Mithila, Vajji and Anga, the history therefore cannot be reduced to a list of feature films.

mai.title: सिनेमा, भिडियो आ अभिलेखित प्रदर्शन
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “सिनेमा, भिडियो आ अभिलेखित प्रदर्शन” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: The moving image altered the relation between performance and presence
Cinema halls connected regional audiences to national and global screen cultures before local film industries matured
Early Maithili cinema has to be reconstructed from contradictory dates and incomplete surviving material
Kanyadan linked literary prestige to cinema but also exposed the multilingual reality of screen production

en.title: Newspapers and Public Debate
en.summary: Newspapers created a distinctive arena of public life because they turned events, arguments and institutional claims into serial, datable objects that could circulate beyond a meeting, court, market or village. In Mithila, Vajji and Anga, however, the newspaper cannot be separated neatly from the literary magazine. Early Maithili periodicals carried essays, letters, language debates, social reform, institutional proceedings and current affairs beside poetry and fiction.

mai.title: समाचारपत्र आ सार्वजनिक बहस
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “समाचारपत्र आ सार्वजनिक बहस” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: A newspaper is an institution of selection before it is a record of events
The regional public sphere was multilingual from the beginning
Early Maithili journalism grew through periodicals before a durable daily-news industry existed
Mithila Mihir became the most consequential early forum because it linked serial print to organised politics and culture

en.title: Sahitya Akademi, Academies and Institutional Canon Formation
en.summary: Literary institutions do more than honour books after they have been written. They create recurring procedures through which manuscripts become editions, editions become eligible books, books become award candidates, authors become representatives of a language, and selected works enter libraries, syllabi, translation circuits and public memory. In that sense an academy is not merely a building or a committee. It is a mechanism for allocating attention.

mai.title: साहित्य अकादमी, अकादमीसभ आ संस्थागत क्यानन-निर्माण
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “साहित्य अकादमी, अकादमीसभ आ संस्थागत क्यानन-निर्माण” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: An institution does not discover a canon; it produces one through repeated acts of selection
Canon, archive, curriculum and award are related but analytically distinct
Sahitya Akademi was designed as an autonomous national literary institution rather than a ministry department
Maithili’s Sahitya Akademi award history begins in 1966, before constitutional scheduling

en.title: Women Writers and Alternative Literary Publics
en.summary: Women’s writing cannot be reconstructed by beginning with prize lists and then working backward. In Mithila, Vajji, Anga and Madhesh, women participated in literary culture through a much wider range of forms: household storytelling, songs attached to marriage and ritual, letters, diaries, memoir, school and association writing, periodicals, fiction, translation, performance, painting-linked narrative, radio and recorded speech, and now digital publication.

mai.title: महिला लेखिका आ वैकल्पिक साहित्यिक सार्वजनिकता
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “महिला लेखिका आ वैकल्पिक साहित्यिक सार्वजनिकता” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Women’s literary history begins before the category of the published woman author
Archival absence is produced by institutions as much as by silence
Household storytelling formed a counter-public without becoming a separate society
Song traditions preserve women’s voices but require performance-sensitive reading

en.title: Videha and Digital Literary Culture
en.summary: Videha is useful to social and cultural history not simply because it publishes Maithili literature online, but because its development exposes the infrastructures required to make a small-language literary public durable on the web. A digital journal must repeatedly solve problems that print can hide inside established institutions: how writers submit work, how issues acquire dates and sequence, how old material remains findable, how scripts render across devices, how audio and images are preserved, how readers…

mai.title: विदेह आ डिजिटल साहित्यिक संस्कृति
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “विदेह आ डिजिटल साहित्यिक संस्कृति” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Digital literary culture is an infrastructure of circulation, not merely literature placed on a screen
Videha’s chronology demonstrates why born-digital institutions often have more than one legitimate beginning
The fortnightly rhythm turned a website into a temporal institution
Email submission lowered geographic barriers while retaining a recognisable editorial gate

en.title: Digital Archives and Cultural Preservation
en.summary: Digital preservation changes the scale at which the social and cultural history of Mithila, Vajji and Anga can be reconstructed. Manuscripts dispersed among families, institutional records, fragile newspapers, cassette recordings, photographs, field notes, performance video and born-digital literary material can now be copied and connected without physically gathering every original in one repository.

mai.title: डिजिटल अभिलेखागार आ सांस्कृतिक संरक्षण
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “डिजिटल अभिलेखागार आ सांस्कृतिक संरक्षण” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Digitisation and digital preservation answer different historical problems
The physical original remains evidence after a digital surrogate is created
Selection is the first act of canon formation in a digital archive
Provenance is the bridge between a file and a historical source

en.title: Unicode, Tirhuta and Technological Recognition
en.summary: The technological history of Maithili cannot be reduced to the arrival of computers or the spread of mobile phones. For a language with a historic script, the decisive question is whether text can be represented as text rather than merely displayed as pictures of letters. Tirhuta, also called Mithilakshara and Maithili script, illustrates the difference.

mai.title: यूनिकोड, तिरहुता आ प्रौद्योगिक मान्यता
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “यूनिकोड, तिरहुता आ प्रौद्योगिक मान्यता” विषयक मुद्रण, रेडियो, सिनेमा, समाचार, अकादमी, महिला लेखन, डिजिटल संस्कृति आ लिपि-प्रौद्योगिकीक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Script, language and technology are different historical categories
Tirhuta as a writing tradition of Mithila
Devanagari dominance and the problem of technological substitution
Early digitisation through legacy fonts
